To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the size spectra and composition of DOM colloids in the Mississippi River and its estuarine plume were characterized and that the colloids exhibited different estuarine mixing behaviors, which were consistent with different sources and chemical compositions.
the size and composition of DOM are controlled by land use hydrological condition water residence time and physicochemical processes in estuaries.
different size fractions of DOM behave differently during estuarine and oceanic mixing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions.
understanding the role of estuaries as chemical reactors in the coastal ocean, and the importance of the size and composition of DOM to its fate and function in the coastal ocean.
the colloidal composition, size partitioning, and estuarine behavior of optically active DOM, which is a key factor controlling the optical properties of coastal waters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

estuarine mixing processes are a major factor controlling the size distribution and composition of optically active DOM in the lower MR estuary and SLB, and the removal of chromophoric and protein like DOM is a major factor controlling their abundance in the northern Gulf of Mex ico coastal waters.
estuarine and riverine DOM in the northern Gulf of Mex ico is composed of different components with different sources and different estuarine mixing behaviors.
the size partitioning of DOM in the estuary and coastal waters is controlled by both the composition of the DOM and its interaction with the environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the estuarine removal of colloidal chromatic DOM is likely due to the removal of the smaller size fraction (0.5 1.2 nm).
the size partitioning and estuarine behavior of colloidal DOM are determined by a combination of physiochemical processes, DOM composition, and hydrological conditions in the river basin.

the colloidal size spectra and composition of optically active DOM are strongly influenced by land use and hydrological conditions in river basins, and by estuarine mixing processes in estuarine systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the colloidal size spectra and mixing behavior of different DOM components can be significantly different in the estuarine and marine environment, and that the size fractionation of DOM can be a useful tool for studying the estuarine dynamics and biogeochemistry of DOM.

the colloidal composition of optically active DOM is highly variable in estuarine systems and that the estuarine removal and mixing behavior of DOM can be highly variable depending on the DOM composition.
the size fractionation of DOM is an important consideration in understanding the estuarine biogeochemistry of DOM.
